clue.text: Son wears leather, inspired by father — it's in the blood

indicators.note: to be inspired is to be breathed into, so the father takes the rest into his middle

parts.note: PA is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: the son is inside the leather as a wearer is inside clothes

parts.note: to leather someone is to thrash them, as is to lam

explanation.surface: A boy in leathers takes after his dad: it runs in the family blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leather' looks like the material but is a verb meaning to beat; 'wears' and 'inspired by' are two nested container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale fluid part of blood in which the cells float.

clue.text: Old driver to praise quality of road

parts.note: to laud is to praise
an A-road is a main road, so A grades its quality

explanation.surface: A retired motorist sings the praises of a smooth road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A, B and so on, so the main-road class A is the road's quality. Niki Lauda was a Formula One world champion who has since died.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was a racing champion of the past, so a former driver by name.

clue.text: Using scornful language, artist's upset by actors in charge

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the word upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist, plus the 'S
a cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An artist is put out by the actors running the show and speaks cuttingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RA'S to SAR at the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, scornful speech, so a sarcastic person is using it.

clue.text: Sun maybe leading with article on US city, regardless of circumstances

indicators.note: the day is led by the other pieces, which come above it in the down entry

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
NY is New York
Sun is short for Sunday, one example of a day

explanation.surface: A sunny day starts with a newspaper article about New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun maybe' looks like the newspaper or the star but is an abbreviated weekday, DAY by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something will happen any day means it will come whatever the situation, at no fixed time.

clue.text: Like to probe those people over battle site

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so these letters are pushed inside the other word

parts.note: THEM means those people
A LA means in the style of, like
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something like a probe into those people over a famous battle site.
explanation.walkthrough: A LA, 'in the manner of', goes inside THEM, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1836 siege of a Texan mission fortress in San Antonio is famous as a battle.

clue.text: Pianist has split pants in rock spoof

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of

explanation.surface: A pianist's trousers rip during a send-up of a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like the anagram signal with 'pants' as fodder; in fact 'split' is fodder and 'pants' (slang for awful) signals the anagram. The 1984 film mocks heavy-metal bands.
explanation.definitionFit: The film is a mockumentary sending up a fictional heavy-metal band on tour.

clue.text: Organised occasion with fish served late in day for Pope?

parts.note: an event is a planned occasion
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A church function serving fish to the Pope late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pope is Alexander Pope the poet, not the pontiff: poets use this old word for evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic word for evening is the late part of the day as an eighteenth-century poet might call it.

clue.text: Shelf life primarily shown on rim

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of life is used

parts.note: the rim of something is its edge

explanation.surface: A shelf's life is mainly spent showing what sits on its rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow flat projection from a wall or cliff is a shelf of rock or wood.

clue.text: Stratagem to get staff to go to work

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
an oeuvre is a work, or the body of works, of an artist

explanation.surface: A ploy to get employees to turn up at their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a noun but is the verb to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever move or scheme to outwit someone is a ruse or stratagem.

clue.text: Floor covering someone pursued, rejecting cream mostly

parts.note: a quarry is the hunted one

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the letters are read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite

explanation.surface: Someone on the run turns down most of the cream on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ELITE to ELIT, and 'rejecting' turns that to TILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unglazed fired-clay tiles are a common hard flooring material.

clue.text: Racket flick ultimately might produce this

definitions.text: Racket flick ultimately might produce this

parts.note: a racket is a din, a loud noise

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of flick is used

explanation.surface: A deft flick of a racket can produce a gentle drop shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' is noise in the wordplay but a tennis racket in the whole-clue reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A softly played drop shot just over the net, as in tennis or pickleball, comes from a delicate flick of the wrist.

clue.text: In very dry area, note regulars in ram-raid going after spirit

indicators.note: the note and the picked letters follow the spirit, coming after it in the answer

parts.note: KA is the Egyptian notion of the spirit or soul
LAH is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: regular letters means every other one, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: In a desert region, a note is found in a ram-raid following some liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like a drink but is the Egyptian KA. 'regulars in' picks ARI from the alternate letters of ram-raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a large semi-arid desert in southern Africa.

clue.text: Greek goddess, flanked by banks of Tigris in ancient city

indicators.note: to be flanked is to have something at each side, so the goddess sits between
the banks of a river are its two edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess stands on both banks of the Tigris in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tigris is in Mesopotamia, but the city is in Egypt or Greece; its outer letters T and S go round HEBE.
explanation.definitionFit: There were two famous historic cities of the name, one in Egypt and one in Greece.

clue.text: Image of thief running riot hard to remove

indicators.note: running riot means going wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder
removing means taking a letter out of the shuffled word

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A police picture of a thief on the rampage proves hard to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' scrambles THIEF; 'to remove' takes out H, leaving the letters EFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Police make a computer-generated likeness of a suspect, a picture built from witness descriptions.

clue.text: Heard cry from golfer swinging towards section of wood

indicators.note: heard means the words are said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a golfer shouts fore as a warning; bi is slang for bisexual, swinging both ways; to means towards

explanation.surface: A shout from a golfer in mid-swing is heard heading for the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' is not the golf swing but bisexual, BI. Said aloud, FORE BI TO gives the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber cut to a cross-section of four inches by two is a standard piece of sawn wood.

clue.text: Number two of sergeants given case

indicators.note: two of means the first two letters are taken from the word

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: The second-in-command of the sergeants is handed a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but a thing that numbs, a common crossword trick; 'Number two' looks like a phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A calming drug dulls feeling, making it something that numbs the senses.

clue.text: Sort of aquaculture tutor trained to join force on inlet

indicators.note: in a down entry, the force sits on top of the inlet
training something reshapes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics
an arm of the sea is an inlet

explanation.surface: A trained tutor joins the forces stationed on a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges TUTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish-rearing in ponds or tanks is one kind of aquaculture, cultivating aquatic animals.

clue.text: Method of presenting film in camera rolls

indicators.note: rolling something tumbles it about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A projection technique for a film being shot as the camera rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like film rolling in the camera but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A widescreen projection system of the 1950s used three projectors to show a film on a curved screen.

clue.text: Half of South African cricket club welcome trousers in green

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters

parts.note: a Zulu is a South African person

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the greeting takes the other word inside

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: Half a South African cricket club welcomes visitors in green trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb, to pocket: HI holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The courgette is a green vegetable, and greens are vegetables in general.

clue.text: Beef stock in cooker, from five to ten

indicators.note: five and ten are the Roman numerals V and X, so the one is swapped for the other

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to simmer beef stock for five to ten minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef stock' looks like soup but means cattle kept for beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle, kept as livestock for meat, are beef animals on the hoof.

clue.text: The British and Irish cook odd fish

parts.note: said by a British setter, we means the British people
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: Britons and Irish together cook up a strange fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd fish' sounds culinary but is the idiom for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange or eccentric person is called a queer or odd fish in British idiom.

clue.text: Dim pupil once taking time with exercise

parts.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A slow-witted former pupil takes his time over the exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slow to understand is thick, a sense of dim.

clue.text: Former athlete, losing sex appeal, in bar providing security

indicators.note: losing means these letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: Usain Bolt is a retired Jamaican sprinter

explanation.surface: A former sprinter, no longer sexy, ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: SA and the clue's own 'in' both go, leaving U and BOLT.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped bolt with threaded ends is used to fasten pipes and fixings securely.

clue.text: Casualty admits Rupert, having fallen in hole

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the casualty department takes the patient inside

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is the casualty department of a hospital

indicators.note: something that has fallen in has collapsed, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A hospital takes in Rupert after he tumbled into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the casualty ward is A and E. 'having fallen in' scrambles RUPERT to PERTUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or gap, as in a camera lens, is a hole.

clue.text: Wolfgang's agreed to pass port and wine

indicators.note: the yes passes the port and so comes after it in the down entry

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port
ja is German for yes, as Wolfgang would say

explanation.surface: A German agrees to pass the port and wine round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing the port is a dinner-table custom; here 'port' is a harbour city and Wolfgang stands for any German.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Rose produces this extravagant ring

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A rose gives a flamboyant ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' could be a past tense; it is the flower, whose essential oil this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar or otto of roses is the fragrant oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Eric's mate knocked back roll, holding onto key that belongs to car?

indicators.note: the key holds onto the front of the rest, coming first

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
Ern was Ernie Wise, comic partner of Eric Morecambe

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of names

explanation.surface: A comedian's partner downs a bread roll while clutching his car key.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a famous British comedy double act; Eric called his partner Ern. 'knocked back' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo-like generator under the bonnet charges a vehicle's battery.

clue.text: Smell round side of lamppost affected where terrier potentially goes

parts.note: BO is body odour
O is round in shape

indicators.note: a side is an edge, here the last letter of lamppost

parts.note: camp means affected, theatrically mannered

explanation.surface: A dog sniffs round a lamppost where a terrier might go.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrier is a crossword term for a Territorial Army soldier, who might do basic training; the surface wants a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A short intensive training course for recruits is where a new reservist goes.

clue.text: A Sound of Music retro production, initially shown in thespian circles

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
the letter is shown inside the actor

parts.note: a ham is an overacting thespian

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of production

parts.note: two O shapes look like circles

explanation.surface: A revival production of The Sound of Music staged by theatre groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' reverses HAPM plus OO; the musical's title is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep rhythmic noise of a brass band's tuba is a sound of music.
